column2: NOT PORTED, AND IT IS THEIR DEFAULT
column3: cuML olsFit defaults to algo=0, one-sided Jacobi SVD. Normal equations SQUARE the condition number, so lstsqEig loses about twice the digits on an ill-conditioned design. sklearn's LinearRegression uses LAPACK gelsd, also an SVD route, so this difference belongs in any accuracy comparison
ridge is lstsqEig with alpha added to the eigenvalues before inverting. Cheap once wanted

column2: NOT PORTED, AND fit_intercept IS ON THEIR DEFAULT PATH
column3: LinearRegression(fit_intercept=True) is cuML's PYTHON DEFAULT (linear_regression.pyx:309), so their default fit is preProcessData -> lstsqEig -> postProcessData, not lstsqEig alone. preProcessData centers X by column means and y by its mean (preprocess.cuh:98,100,115,117); postProcessData sets intercept = mean(y) - mu_X . coef and UNDOES both centerings in place (preprocess.cuh:148-176). ols_fit refuses fit_intercept and defaults it False, i.e. it mirrors the fit_intercept=False branch, which on their side also sets *intercept = 0 (ols.cuh:156). core/column_stats.mojo already has the kernels. normalize is only reachable with fit_intercept and is the meanvar/colNorm arm at preprocess.cuh:76-108
logistic and softmax regression, 2737 lines. An LBFGS/OWL-QN solver with line search, not a linear-algebra routine. See glm/README.md on why its GPU upside is also smaller

column2: PORTED WITH AN ABSOLUTE THRESHOLD, RECORDED AS A DEVIATION
column3: `OLS_NONZERO_THRESH` is 1.0e-10 and is compared against an eigenvalue of A^T A, a quantity that scales with the SQUARE of the data and with n_rows. MEASURED (check_ols_rank_guard_is_absolute): the same 4096x8 design has rank 8 at scale 1 and rank 0 at scale 2^-24, i.e. the same design in different units returns the zero model.
